title: Marrero's bass drum and the over-recorded drums on Dr. Jazz
summary: Martyn asks about the funeral sequence and why the drums sound loud; Watkins blames the engineer's vocal mic.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Well, it's on these records. Something I was going to ask you. Remember on this, these disc jockeys you made? Yeah. And you made this funeral sequence on there? Yeah. When Lawrence plays the bass drum. Did he have his own bass drum there? Or was he playing... No, he had his own bass drum. Yeah, he brought his own bass drum.

Yeah. And he had his own bass drum. But there was some other place... There was some other place that he used my bass drum on a sequence like that. I forgot where it's at. But there was no recording of it. But see, that wasn't on the recording. That was his own, that was his own little bass drum he had. Yeah. And you had your regular snare drum on that?
Yeah, my regular snare drum, yeah. You were sitting there playing your regular snare drum.
And I had my belt and all. Oh yeah, you were sitting there. Because Nick had told us to bring them along with us, you know? Yeah. Yeah, I get you.

And still on these records, well, on this one, someone I'll be meaning to ask you. Where is it? Is he on that one, Dr. Jazz? Uh-huh. Well, you sing on that. Yeah. And on that, the drums is terribly seem to be over recorded, you know? They seem to be loud around the rest. Yeah, yeah it was.

You figure that's, yeah. Yeah. You know that guy, he had that mic. Mm-hmm. See, it's one of the tall mics, you know? Yeah. Because he was up on the stand. Yeah. And he had it protruding too close. Mm-hmm. Because see, I was right in the center. See, George, George and, uh, Howard and Jim was on this side of me. Yeah, that's on the right hand side. And, uh, Elton was on that side. Mm-hmm. And drag and drag was on this side of me. Right. On the left. See, well, naturally, he was picking up more volume with that drum than anything else.
I guess he had it near for you to sing.

Because if you notice in particular, where I take a drum on, drum solo, on Maman on loud, you notice that roll kind of gets offbeat. Yeah. Yeah. And I didn't like that too much. No. See, but what I was gonna do, I couldn't tell him to retake it, because I didn't know how it came out. Yeah, yeah. But I do know he had that mic extended too far.
Up on that stage. If he'd have stayed out where he was, like this stage here. Yeah. And the mic would be over there, and I'd be back here where I'm at. Yeah. Well, it wouldn't pick me up too much.

Mm-hmm. You see? So, for— Just at the right bottom. Yeah. For the people at the front, I mean, the drum, where you was playing on that, that wouldn't have sounded no louder than usual. No, no, no. Just playing— Just playing— It was just that mic was picking it up. Yeah. I guess the mic was there for you to sing the vocal on.

Yeah, that's right. It was there for me to sing the vocal. Instead of him getting it back when it come from my solo, well, he just left it stay right there, and all I was doing was picking up that that pressure on the drums that I was making.
